evidence.text: Alumina prices rose through Q3, which helps the alumina segment beyond the company's +$10M sequential outlook, since that outlook holds prices flat. Rio Tinto's Q3 review (2026-10-14) says FOB Australia alumina rose 8% during Q3 to $355/t. Platts puts the Q2 average at $307.42/t, and SMM recorded $346-356/t trades on 5-6 August for September loading. So the Q3 average API was roughly $30-40/t above Q2's. Consensus models third-party alumina sales down 28.8% YoY ($599M, Zacks).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 the alumina segment lost $96M (Pinjarra, energy contracts) and the stock fell 6.13%, a reaction the sweep ties to the alumina guide cut and South32 overhang. Over the 7 prints in the baseline only 2 rose, so good quarter-level news has not reliably been paid.
evidence.why_not_priced: Alcoa's own Q3 alumina bridge (+$10M) excludes price, and Rio's Q3 review with the quarter-end price landed one day before this print. If this were priced, consensus third-party alumina revenue would not still sit at -28.8% YoY and the stock would not be making new lows on the aluminium price alone. The CFO did say on 10 September that prices had rebounded to about $350, so some analysts will have it.
evidence.independence: Platts Q2 average of $307.42/t (https://www.alcircle.com/news/q2-2026-sees-oversupply-weighing-on-fob-australia-alumina-prices-118154) and SMM's $346/t FOB WA trade on 2026-08-06 (https://news.metal.com/newscontent/104049234-30000-mt-alumina-traded-at-346mt-fob-western-australia-for-september-2026-loading) are independent of Rio. evidence.text: At the Barclays conference on 2026-09-14 (mid-quarter, two days before the Fed hike), CEO Van Saun did not cut any number. He let stand the moderator's framing that full-year NII will exceed the original +10-12%, called the Q4 move into the 3.22-3.27% NIM range 'a pretty big uptick', said 'I wouldn't say spreads are compressing at this point', said a hike adds about 1bp of NIM in Q4 because Citizens is asset-sensitive, and named capital markets 'the star of the show for the next 6 quarters'. Two days later, at the same conference, Huntington cut its 2026 NII growth from 39-43% to ~35% and its 2027 EPS on deposit competition, and fell 5.55%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last two prints with a beat and the guide held both rallied: +4.61% on 2026-07-16 (EPS $1.30 vs $1.25, Q3 NII guide +2.5-3.5%) and +7.11% on 2026-01-21 (baseline). The prints that were in line moved about -0.2% to -1.8%.
evidence.why_not_priced: The remarks are public, but the stock has fallen about 5.6% over 20 days along with the group (KRE about -11% from mid-August) and the sell-side has cut targets into the print. That treats CFG as if it carried Huntington's deposit-margin problem. If the market had priced CFG's swap-driven NIM path (about 7bp of 2H tailwind from terminated swaps, which is mechanical and not deposit-dependent), CFG would have held up better than the group and the targets would not have been cut. This is a reaffirmation of the company's own guide, so most of the value is a guide held rather than raised, and it is sized small.
evidence.independence: Huntington's contrasting cut on 2026-09-16: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/huntington-cut-outlook-fed-hiked-234006771.html. The swap-driven NIM mechanics are from the Q2 call: https://gloom.sh/stocks/cfg/transcripts/q2-2026.

This is a peer proxy, not CFG's own number, so it is sized small, and the peer stock reactions argue the market has already absorbed it.

evidence.text: PNC's capital markets and advisory revenue (it owns Harris Williams, the closest public read on middle-market M&A advisory) fell 25% q/q to $433M in Q3 2026, flat year on year. JPMorgan's CFO said dealmaking slowed in late September, with deals delayed rather than cancelled. WTW counts mid-sized deals as flat to softer while mega deals carried value. The consensus for CFG's capital markets fees is $159.1M, +4% q/q, after a record Q2 that was up 14% q/q.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fee income, led by capital markets, drove the Q2 2026 beat (+4.61%). In July, CFG's Ted Swimmer said he expected M&A to pick up 'into the fourth quarter and into next year' and not in Q3. PNC guided Q4 capital markets +15% and its stock was +0.66% pre-market despite the -25% q/q.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Zacks line consensus still has CFG capital markets rising 4% q/q off a record Q2. If the PNC read-through were priced, that line would have been revised to flat or down. Net of the rest of the company: capital markets is about 7% of revenue, so a 15% miss on the line is about $24M pre-tax, roughly $0.04 of EPS (~3% of the bar), and NII (about 72% of revenue) would have to come in at the top of its guide to cover it. The likely Q4 fee guide-up (PNC +15%) softens the reaction, which is why this is sized below the EPS arithmetic.

That is about 3x its Q3 2025 figure of $558M and in line with its Q2 2026 $1.72B. TRV's cats as a share of Allstate's were 0.72 in Q3'25 ($402M/$558M), 0.61 in Q1'26 ($761M/$1.24B) and 0.30 in Q2'26 ($518M/$1.72B). Applied to $1.65B, that gives a TRV Q3 cat range of about $500M-$1.2B, centred near $900M-1.0B. The consensus combined ratio of 92.1 (vs 87.3, which had 3.6 pts of cats) implies roughly $0.9-1.0B, so the proxy brackets the bar. The lean is slightly favourable because in Q2 TRV came in at 0.30 of Allstate and beat a $5.16-5.41 consensus with $10.04.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Cats drive TRV's surprises. Q2'26: cats $518M vs $927M, core EPS $10.04 vs ~$5.2-5.4 consensus, stock +9.22%. Q3'25: cats $402M vs $939M, $8.14 vs ~$6.30, stock -2.92%. Q1'26: cats $761M vs $2.27B, $7.71 vs $7.08, stock -0.16%. So a light-cat beat has paid in only 1 of 3 recent quarters.
evidence.why_not_priced: Allstate's number was public about 3.5 hours before the baseline seal, and July and August ($1.43B) since 2026-09-17, so the industry level is in the price; Zacks' estimate rose 1.5% in the last week. What is not priced is TRV's share of the industry loss, which has swung from 0.30 to 0.72 of Allstate. If the market had settled on the low ratio, consensus would sit well above $7.36.
evidence.independence: Allstate July/August release (https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20654972-august-2026-monthly-release) is the same series. TRV ratios are from TRV's own releases: Q1'26 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/86312/000008631226000110/a991pressrelease33126.htm; Q3'25 https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/86312/000008631225000068/a991pressrelease93025.htm; Allstate Q1'26 https://www.allstatenewsroom.com/news/march-2026-monthly-release/.

evidence.text: The quarter's largest SCS event was the 9-12 August 2026 Midwest derecho. Illinois 'bore the brunt': near-90 mph winds in Chicago's south suburbs and NW Indiana, and >1.1M outages in IL/IN/OH. Aon and Gallagher Re put it in the low single-digit billions. Allstate is headquartered in Northbrook, IL and over-indexed to Chicago personal lines, so Allstate's August $748M (about 50% from one wind/hail event) likely overstates the industry share falling on TRV's personal lines. Gallagher Re puts YTD US SCS above $35B by mid-August vs $22-27B at mid-June, so Q3 SCS was about $8-13B. No US hurricane landfalled in Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Same cat line as above. Q2'26 had heavy industry SCS (Allstate $1.72B) yet TRV printed $518M and the stock rose 9.2%.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is a geography inference, not a company number. The sell-side scales from industry and Allstate figures. If the market believed TRV was under-exposed, Q3 consensus would not be $1.24 below the year-ago quarter with a 92 combined ratio.
evidence.independence: Proxy only; TRV has not quantified its derecho exposure. The Allstate August release (https://seekingalpha.com/pr/20654972-august-2026-monthly-release) supports the one-event concentration. Shares the Allstate series with finding 1, so the two together should be read as one cat view.

evidence.text: Commercial pricing kept softening into Q3. CIAB's Q2 2026 survey had overall premiums -2% and commercial property -6.3%, with umbrella +5.3%. Marsh had the US composite -2% in Q2. TRV's own Q2 Business Insurance renewal premium change was 4.8% (7.8% ex national property, flat sequentially), so a further Q3 deceleration in renewal premium change and slower NWP growth is the likely forward read on the call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: After strong headline beats in Q3'25 (-2.9%) and Q1'26 (-0.2%), coverage blamed decelerating pricing and premium growth; the Q1'26 revenue missed by ~$0.5B.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the soft market is the bear case behind the Hold ratings and the MS Underweight. A sharper drop in TRV's own renewal premium change below ~4% ex national property would be new.
evidence.independence: Marsh Q2'26 index -2% US (https://www.reinsurancene.ws/abundant-capacity-and-competition-drive-6-global-commercial-insurance-rate-decline-in-q226-marsh/); TRV Q2 call RPC figures (https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/TRV/Q22026).

evidence.text: Q3 is when TRV books its annual asbestos/environmental reserve review. It took a $277M asbestos charge in Q3'25, which turned Business Insurance prior-year development to $125M unfavorable, and $242M in Q3'24. A similar charge is likely again; whether consensus fully carries it is unclear.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3'25 carried the charge inside a large beat and the stock fell 2.9%. The charge was not cited as the cause.
evidence.why_not_priced: It recurs every year, so it is mostly in the models. Only a materially larger charge, or an added general-liability/commercial-auto strengthening, would be new. The Q2 call said the uncertainty provision from 2024-25 remains in place.
evidence.independence: Q3'24 asbestos charge $242M (https://theinsurer.com/?p=43443). Same company series.
